title: Explore demo data from an instrumented app

blocks.content:
You don't need an instrumented app to see what one looks like in Grafana Cloud. The **Demo Data Dashboards** app installs the telemetry of QuickPizza, a fictional pizza service, into hosted data sources that are free to use and don't count toward your usage. This guide installs the demo and runs a first query against its data.

First, install the QuickPizza demo.
Expand **More apps** in the main menu, then open **Demo Data Dashboards**.

Click **Install the Quick Pizza SRE demo**.

This deploys the demo data sources and dashboards, then refreshes the page.

QuickPizza's telemetry is now in your stack. You have a **QuickPizza** dashboards folder, plus data sources for its metrics, logs, and traces.

Next, open one of the demo's prebuilt dashboards.

That's a prebuilt dashboard on an instrumented app's data. Every panel is a live view of the service's request rates, latencies, and errors, and you didn't build or send anything.

Next, query that data yourself.

Choose **grafanacloud-play-prom** in the picker.

It holds the demo's metrics.
blocks.tooltip: Every query runs against one of your connected data stores. This picker chooses which one.

blocks.content:
Switch the query editor to **Code** mode so you can type the query directly.

If **Code** is already selected, this changes nothing.

Enter `sum(rate(quickpizza_server_http_requests_total[5m]))` in the query field.

QuickPizza's server counts every request it handles. This query turns those counts into a rate per second and adds them up across the whole service.

Click **Run query**.

The line coming back is the service's live request rate, real telemetry from a running, instrumented app.

You queried the metrics of an instrumented app without instrumenting anything yourself.

The dashboard you opened and the query you ran read the same data sources, and you can influence the numbers by visiting the live site at [quickpizza.grafana.fun](https://quickpizza.grafana.fun/). When you have an app of your own to instrument, everything you saw here works the same way on your data.
